title: Owner of FOUND-001 and FOUND-002
description: A foundational story carries no covers, so FOUND-001 is covered by the executable service story and FOUND-002 by the test-gate story.

options.label: Service stories cover FOUND-001 and FOUND-002

title: Option syntax
description: Options take a separate value (--top 3). The --top=3 form is not required; a repeated option is a usage error exit 2.

title: Column name matching
description: Column names for --column and --freq match the trimmed header exactly and case-sensitively; no match exits 3.

title: Stub behavior of cli.Run
description: The foundation has no argument parsing yet, so cli.Run writes 'csvstat: not implemented' to stderr and returns 1. I chose 1 over 0 so the stub cannot pass as a successful run. Replace it when the CLI story lands. Is that acceptable?
system_choice: The foundation has no argument parsing yet, so cli.Run writes 'csvstat: not implemented' to stderr and returns 1. I chose 1 over 0 so the stub cannot pass as a successful run. Replace it when the CLI story lands. Is that acceptable?

title: Where empty-input rejection happens
description: Read returns a nil Header with no error for empty or blank-only input, as the spec requires. Rejection is a separate csvdata.Validate, called by cli after Read and Trim, which returns ErrRejected. Reading and rejecting stay separate, and the input-rejection story still holds. Is that acceptable?
system_choice: Read returns a nil Header with no error for empty or blank-only input, as the spec requires. Rejection is a separate csvdata.Validate, called by cli after Read and Trim, which returns ErrRejected. Reading and rejecting stay separate, and the input-rejection story still holds. Is that acceptable?

title: Unknown --freq column name
description: The specs do not say what happens when the --freq column is not in the header. I exit 2 (usage) with empty stdout and a diagnostic on stderr. Exit 3 would also be defensible as rejected input. Is 2 acceptable, or should this be 3?
system_choice: The specs do not say what happens when the --freq column is not in the header. I exit 2 (usage) with empty stdout and a diagnostic on stderr. Exit 3 would also be defensible as rejected input. Is 2 acceptable, or should this be 3?

title: Non-positive --top with --freq
description: Validation of --top belongs to the usage-errors story, which is not in this block. Until then --top 0 or a negative value lists no rows with exit 0. Confirm that the usage-errors story will reject these with exit 2.
system_choice: Validation of --top belongs to the usage-errors story, which is not in this block. Until then --top 0 or a negative value lists no rows with exit 0. Confirm that the usage-errors story will reject these with exit 2.

title: --column without --freq
description: Column output is not part of this block, so --column keeps the prior behaviour: exit 0 with no output. The profile is written only when neither --column nor --freq is given, as the spec says. Confirm this is acceptable until the column story lands.
